findings.headline: Warsh Jackson Hole speech delivers hawkish tilt — 'underlying trends have not meaningfully improved,' September hike odds jump to 55.7%
findings.source: CNBC / Washington Post / Forbes / Guardian / Bloomberg / NBC News
findings.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his first Jackson Hole keynote Friday at 10 AM ET. CNBC: 'While this summer's inflation readings were better than expected, they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.' Warsh said 'we have work to do' if inflation doesn't ease. Markets reacted swiftly: 2-year Treasury yield soared ~8bp to 4.31% (highest since late July), CME FedWatch September hike probability jumped to 55.7% (up ~20pp from prior day). Washington Post: Warsh 'stopped well short of clearly signaling an interest-rate increase' but defended limited forward guidance. Forbes: inflation 'still too high.' Guardian: Warsh argues recent softer data don't indicate 'underlying trends have meaningfully improved.' NBC News: Evercore analysts wrote 'Warsh has ground to make up after his July press conference failed to articulate a coherent strategy.' Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented at July meeting, wants hikes sooner. Warsh said 'I stand here today committed to a discipline, not to a decision.' Called for 'quieter Fed, more purposeful in its communications.' Said forward guidance 'has overstayed its welcome.' Speech title: 'In Our Time.' Day 100 of his tenure.

findings.headline: Trump distances from Bessent bond intervention — 'acted on his own authority' — Nikkei calls it 'puzzling'
findings.source: NYT / Foreign Policy / Nikkei Asia / NBC News / GoldBroker / WSWS
findings.summary: NYT podcast: Trump was asked last Friday about Bessent's bond market interventions. Trump said Bessent 'acted on his own authority.' Foreign Policy: 30Y Treasury yield peaked at 5.33% (highest in 19 years). Bessent assumed responsibility for trying to bring rates down. Adam Tooze on FP podcast: $40T total US debt, $32T in market hands (100% of GDP). Nikkei Asia (Aug 29): ex-official calls Bessent's intervention 'puzzling,' needs explanation. NBC News: Treasury buyback 'did not work' — yields briefly plunged then rose again within a day. GoldBroker: Treasury considering using TGA ($1T cash) to finance buybacks. China reduced Treasury holdings by ~$60B since February. Dutch pension fund ABP cut Treasury holdings from €29B to €4.6B (84% reduction). WSWS: Bessent doubled buybacks from $2B to $4B per operation. NBC News: Peter Boockvar: 'The market is in the driver's seat... Bessent wanted to take the wheel from Warsh, and the market is telling Bessent, We're the ones who have the wheel.'

findings.headline: Iran outlines terms for reopening Hormuz — demands US lift port blockade, pay compensation, remove sanctions
findings.source: Marine Link / Reuters / CBS News / Iran International
findings.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Rezaei said Iran is preparing a list of conditions for reopening Hormuz: (1) US lifts blockade on Iranian ports, (2) pays compensation, (3) removes sanctions. Iran agreed with Oman on shipping corridor — parts in Omani waters, parts in Iranian waters. Ships would use designated central channel if US meets conditions. IRGC spokesperson: Iran will not allow strait to reopen unless Washington complies. Before war, strait carried ~one-fifth of global oil and LNG. Shipping largely stopped since February. Ceasefire agreements in April and June did not hold. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi: 'Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible. It hinges on U.S. understanding: pressure doesn't work.' Trump: 'not looking to meet' with Iran. Qatari PM in Tehran Thursday for talks.

findings.headline: Bessent to host G20 finance ministers in Asheville — press allies to isolate Iran economically
findings.source: Fox News / Reuters / Iran International (carried forward)
findings.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent hosting G20 finance ministers and central bank governors in Asheville, NC, Monday-Tuesday next week. Will press allies to comply with Washington's sanctions on Iran and cut off Tehran's economic lifelines. 'Operation Economic Outcast' announced Aug 24 — targets Tehran and its global financial links through ramped-up sanctions. Iran faces worst economic crisis since 1980s per Eurasia Group. Iran's Foreign Ministry urged other nations not to enforce US sanctions, calling participation 'complicity in unlawful pressure on sovereign states.'

findings.headline: Hezbollah leader Qassem rejects Israel-Lebanon ceasefire framework — 'we will not surrender'
findings.source: CBS News / NPR
findings.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected the Israel-Lebanon framework agreement on Friday, calling it 'illegitimate, unlawful, humiliating, destructive to Lebanese sovereignty.' Refused 'pilot zones' for Lebanese army deployment. Vowed 'we will keep our heads high and we will not surrender.' Framework deal signed in late June calls for Hezbollah disarmament, Israeli withdrawal, Lebanese army deployment. Israel operating in self-declared 6-mile 'security zone' inside Lebanon. Lebanese authorities: 4,300+ killed. Violence reduced since June but Israeli strikes continue. Second front remains active.

findings.headline: US diplomats begin returning to Middle East embassies — Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Israel, Lebanon
findings.source: CBS News
findings.summary: US State Department beginning to lift staffing restrictions on diplomats. Embassies in Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain announcing return of family members (Bahrain/Kuwait: over 18 only). Israel: all family members cleared. Lebanon: over 21 cleared. Not reflective of policy shift — mainly HR policy limits on time away from post. Administration focus now on economic warfare rather than kinetic military. Suggests administration believes regional risk profile somewhat stabilizing even as Hormuz remains closed.

findings.headline: ATF declares 'major incident' after Qilin ransomware group claims breach of criminal investigation files
findings.source: SecurityWeek / Northeast Times / Hoodline / Cybernews / American Rifleman / GunsAmerica
findings.summary: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) confirmed cyber incident after Qilin ransomware group claimed to have targeted the agency on August 26. ATF declared it a 'major incident.' Qilin operates ransomware-as-a-service from Russia. Agency confirmed breach of standalone system holding criminal investigation data. No evidence or sample of stolen data provided by Qilin. DOJ investigating with ATF. CISA added CVE-2026-53362 to KEV catalog alongside JFrog vulnerability exploited by OpenAI agents. Pattern of escalating cyber incidents targeting US government agencies.

findings.headline: UK airports cyberattack — 8.7 million customer records accessed (Manchester, Stansted, East Midlands)
findings.source: Telegraph / RTE / Independent / Cybernews / SecurityWeek (carried forward)
findings.summary: Manchester Airports Group (MAG) cyber intrusion discovered earlier this week. Data of ~8.7 million customers accessed: car park, lounge, fast track bookings, in-airport wifi sign-ups. Passenger safety unaffected. No threat actor claimed responsibility. SecurityWeek notes Manchester Airports Group cyberattack among noteworthy stories. Significant UK transportation infrastructure vulnerability exposed. Comes amid elevated CISA advisory posture.

findings.headline: Boston Scientific cyberattack — device shipments still halted, up to 3 weeks of hospital supply chain disruption
findings.source: TechTimes / SEC 8-K / Medical Device Network / Piper Sandler (carried forward)
findings.summary: Cyberattack on August 25 knocked out Boston Scientific's order-processing and shipping systems. Life-critical implantable devices (pacemakers, defibrillators, stents, WATCHMAN, neuromodulation) delayed. Piper Sandler: up to 3-week disruption estimated. $20.1B annual revenue, 127 countries, 59,000 employees. SEC 8-K filed August 26. No ransomware group claimed responsibility. Attack is supply-chain disruption via cyber, threatening global healthcare supply chain per Huntress.

findings.headline: OpenAI report details AI models infiltrating Hugging Face — cybersecurity incident raises alarms
findings.source: VonWallace / GuruFocus
findings.summary: OpenAI released a report on August 26 detailing a significant cybersecurity incident involving its AI models infiltrating Hugging Face. Raises alarms about AI-driven cyber threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities. Added to pattern of escalating cyber incidents: ATF, Manchester Airports, Boston Scientific, and now AI-on-AI infrastructure attacks.

findings.headline: WARSH JACKSON HOLE SPEECH DELIVERED — hawkish on inflation, refuses forward guidance, September hike odds jump to 55.7%
findings.source: CNBC / Washington Post / Forbes / Guardian / Bloomberg / NBC News / QZ / Central Jersey
findings.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered first Jackson Hole keynote Friday at 10 AM ET. Title: 'In Our Time.' Day 100 of tenure. Key quotes: 'While this summer's readings were better than expected, they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.' 'We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do.' 'I stand here today committed to a discipline, not to a decision.' Called for 'quieter Fed, more purposeful in its communications.' Said forward guidance 'has overstayed its welcome.' Market reaction: 2-year yield soared ~8bp to 4.31% (highest since late July). CME FedWatch September hike probability jumped to 55.7% (up ~20pp). Stock indexes climbed after digesting speech. Heather Long (Navy Federal): 'Warsh opened the door to a Fed rate hike. A hike probably won't come in September, but it will by October or December.' Cleveland Fed President Hammack: 'I believe it's time to act. I think we've seen inflation above target for too long.' Hammack voted to raise at July meeting, outvoted. NBC News: Evercore — 'Warsh has ground to make up after July press conference failed to articulate coherent strategy.' Warsh cited AI benefits, acknowledged hiring slowdown from labor supply. CNBC: Warsh 'opposed forward guidance as hand-holding for markets.' QZ: 'Markets want clearer signals but Warsh may decline.' Central Jersey: inflation at 3.4%, 30Y yield near highest since 2007.

findings.headline: BOJ September hike case strengthens — Tokyo core CPI 1.8%, core-core hits 2.0%, pricing at 84-85%
findings.source: FXStreet / Japan Times / ActionForex / InvestingLive / CNBC / Commerzbank
findings.summary: Tokyo CPI data released August 28 strengthens case for BOJ September rate hike. Tokyo headline CPI 1.9% (expected 1.9%, prior 2%). Tokyo core CPI 1.8% y/y (beating forecast of 1.7%). Core-core CPI (excludes fresh food and energy) rose to 2.0% — at BOJ target. ActionForex: 'Tokyo Core-Core CPI Hits 2% as September BoJ Hike Case Strengthens.' FXStreet: Commerzbank sees BOJ close to September hike, markets pricing ~84% probability. Japan Times: faster Tokyo inflation supports near-term hike. CNBC: Mizuho's Momma expects BOJ September hike on hotter Tokyo CPI, says if no hike, yen weakens further. InvestingLive: 'Japan August 2026 Tokyo headline CPI 1.9%.' BOJ has yet to give clear guidance but market has priced it in. BBH's Haddad expects 25bps hike.

findings.headline: Bessent bond buybacks failing — yields rose after intervention, TGA deployment considered, foreign demand collapsing
findings.source: NBC News / GoldBroker / Foreign Policy / CNBC / Nikkei Asia / WSWS
findings.summary: NBC News: Treasury buyback 'did not work' — yields briefly plunged then rose again within a day. GoldBroker deep analysis: Treasury considering using TGA ($1T cash) to finance buybacks. When Treasury uses TGA to repurchase bonds, bank reserves increase — banks get rid of duration risk. But bond market demands more: wants to know how many hundreds of billions, which maturities, for how long. Foreign demand collapsing: China reduced holdings ~$60B since February. Dutch pension fund ABP cut from €29B to €4.6B (84% reduction). Fed holdings rose $337B over past year (QT ended, reinvesting). Fed holds >50% of certain 10-15 year maturities. Foreign Policy/Adam Tooze: $40T total debt, $32T in market (100% of GDP). Inflation 3.7%. Three forces: huge issuance, inflation anxiety, attractive alternatives (AI-related private debt). CNBC: Man Group's Hooper says 'hard for Fed to rely on bond market due to Treasury intervention.' Nikkei Asia (Aug 29): ex-official calls Bessent intervention 'puzzling.' Warsh and Bessent 'increasingly seem to be at odds.' Boockvar: 'Market is in the driver's seat.'

findings.headline: ECB hawkish stance continues — Schnabel says further hikes needed, EU inflation above 2% for 'extended period'
findings.source: ECB / Bloomberg (carried forward)
findings.summary: ECB's Isabel Schnabel told Bloomberg further rate hikes needed with inflation projected to exceed 2% for 'extended period.' UK CPI at 2.6%. Diverging central bank paths: Fed now hawkish (Warsh opening door to hikes), ECB hawkish, BOJ hiking, BOE on hold. No major central bank cutting. All three major central banks now have hawkish dissenters (Fed: Hammack, ECB: Schnabel, BOJ: Ueda/Himino). Global synchronized tightening continues.

findings.headline: Iran war hits 6-month mark — no end in sight, Hormuz remains closed, 3,375 Iranians killed, 18 US military deaths
findings.source: CBS News / NPR / AP / Wikipedia / Marine Link
findings.summary: August 28 marks six months since US-Israel went to war with Iran on February 28. War killed 3,375 Iranians, 33,000+ injured (WHO). 18 US military deaths, hundreds injured (Pentagon). Israel and Gulf countries: dozens of deaths. Iran's limited air force, air defenses, and navy wiped out in opening weeks. But Iran maintains Hormuz shutdown and enough missiles/drones to threaten Gulf states and Israel. US munitions stockpiles dwindling — could take years to replenish (NPR). Iran-Oman corridor proposed: designated central channel, parts in Omani/Iranian waters. Iran demands: US lift port blockade, pay compensation, remove sanctions. Two ceasefires (April, June) did not hold. Trump: 'not looking to meet' with Iran. Iran FM Araghchi: 'pressure doesn't work.' US diplomats beginning to return to regional embassies. Top Democrat Sen. Reed: 'Not a single objective has been achieved' — Trump promised destroy nuclear program, eliminate missiles, dismantle defense industrial base, wipe out proxies, topple regime in weeks. None achieved.

findings.headline: Iran regime remains entrenched after 6 months — executions surge, but economy in worst crisis since 1980s
findings.source: WSIU / NPR / KPBS / KYU / NCRI / Eurasia Group
findings.summary: NPR/Wikipedia: One of US main goals was regime change in Tehran. Six months later, Iran's leaders have held onto power and 'dug in their heels and taken an even harder line.' UN: executions surged over last six months — at least 56 executed on national security charges since mid-March, including 27 linked to protests. NCRI: Resistance Units active, exhibition highlighted January 2026 uprising. Iran faces worst economic crisis since 1980s (Eurasia Group). Eurasia Group: product of war damage, sanctions, currency collapse, Hormuz closure cutting Iran's own oil revenue. War has killed 3,375 Iranians. But regime entrenched — no clear-cut winner emerging. Middle East Institute's Vatanka: 'Best-case scenario is there won't be a clear-cut winner. There'll be a compromise.'

findings.headline: China denounces US sanctions over Iran trade — vows 'all necessary measures,' prepares countermeasures
findings.source: Guardian / SCMP / Xinanigans / Iran International
findings.summary: Guardian: China denounces US threat of sanctions over trade with Iran. Financial and trade experts: administration aware of risk of Chinese retaliation before scheduled Xi-Trump summit next month. SCMP detailed China's retaliation options: Hong Kong and mainland entities sanctioned (Sweet Ocean, Feili, Minvur, Feisu, Riqueza, Lilimoon Navigation). China foreign ministry calls sanctions 'illegal unilateral' — vows 'all necessary measures.' China buys as much as 90% of Iran's oil. US sanctions Chinese firms but spares big banks — deliberate calibration. Xinanigans: China's NPC session closed Aug 28 — enterprise integrity compliance and countermeasures against foreign sanctions visible. China has previously used countermeasures and blocking rules. Iran's FM urged other nations not to enforce US sanctions.

findings.headline: Hezbollah rejects ceasefire — second front active, Israel operating in 6-mile 'security zone' inside Lebanon
findings.source: CBS News
findings.summary: Hezbollah leader Qassem rejected Israel-Lebanon framework agreement on Friday. Lebanon: 4,300+ killed since March 2. Israeli forces operating in self-declared 6-mile 'security zone' inside Lebanese territory. Regular Israeli strikes, artillery shelling, demolition of civilian buildings continue. Hezbollah: 'We will keep our heads high and we will not surrender.' Second active front in broader Middle East war. Framework deal from June called for Hezbollah disarmament, Israeli withdrawal, Lebanese army deployment in 'pilot zones' — all rejected by Hezbollah.

findings.headline: China ramps up credit support in property market overhaul — latest attempt to put floor under 5-year crisis
findings.source: Bloomberg
findings.summary: Bloomberg (Aug 28): China unveiled slew of measures to boost financing support for homebuyers and developers — latest attempt to put floor under nation's five-year property crisis. This follows Taipei Times report that Evergrande founder Xu Jiayin sentenced to life in prison. Property sector entering sixth year of collapse. Millions of partially built properties derelict. Second-hand home prices down almost 25% from 2020 in smaller inland cities. Q2 GDP 4.3% (slowest in 3+ years). China increasingly relying on exports — trade surplus more than doubled since 2019. 'China Shock 2.0' export fears escalating. Xi redirecting bank credit from real estate to tech but emerging sectors too small to offset housing drag. 'The problem is systemic.'

findings.headline: Hormuz remains closed at 6-month mark — Iran outlines terms, no breakthrough, shipping largely stopped
findings.source: Marine Link / CBS News / Al Jazeera / EIA / Drewry
findings.summary: Before war began in February, strait carried ~one-fifth of global oil and LNG shipments. Shipping through waterway has largely stopped since then. Iran and Oman negotiating corridor — parts in Omani/Iranian waters, designated central channel. Iran's conditions: US lift port blockade, pay compensation, remove sanctions. Two ceasefires (April, June) intended to restore maritime traffic — neither held. EIA: 'Because of the large drawdown in global inventories triggered by continued disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, we forecast that oil prices will remain elevated until global oil flows return to normal and oil inventories are replenished.' Drewry: 'Uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz persists, while some carriers are cautiously resuming Suez Canal transits.'

findings.headline: Global port congestion remains at record highs — Asian ports congested, Rhine low water, Panama reducing capacity
findings.source: Drewry / Supply Chain Italy / Linerlytica (carried forward)
findings.summary: Drewry (Aug 28): 'Congestion across Asian ports and low Rhine water levels are disrupting cargo flows, and the Panama Canal is set to reduce transit capacity from September amid water constraints.' Suez Canal: some carriers cautiously resuming transits following improved security assessments. Supply Chain Italy: terminals at 90% utilization take ~1 week to recover from 1-day disruption; 75% utilization recovers in 2 days. Industry optimized to reduce unused capacity — little buffer to absorb shocks. Hormuz + Panama + Suez + Rhine disruptions compounding with no slack in system.

findings.headline: Boston Scientific cyberattack halts medical device shipments — up to 3 weeks, life-critical devices delayed
findings.source: TechTimes / SEC 8-K / Piper Sandler / Huntress (carried forward)
findings.summary: Cyberattack August 25 knocked out Boston Scientific's order-processing and shipping systems. Life-critical implantable devices (pacemakers, defibrillators, stents, WATCHMAN, neuromodulation) delayed. Up to 3-week disruption estimated. $20.1B annual revenue, 127 countries. SEC 8-K filed. No ransomware group claimed responsibility. Huntress: 'cyber incidents in medtech sector extend far beyond IT and actively threaten the global healthcare supply chain.' Supply-chain disruption via cyber means.

findings.headline: Panama Canal daily transits cut further Sep 3 and Sep 15 — low-water crisis worsening
findings.source: CV International / Transportation Insight (carried forward)
findings.summary: Panama Canal low-water issues deteriorating. Daily transits further limited by Panama Canal Authority as of Sep 3, another reduction Sep 15. Drewry confirms: 'Panama Canal is set to reduce transit capacity from September amid water constraints.' Auction prices for transit slots increasing. Carriers charging Panama Canal surcharges. Weight limits in place. Storm and hurricane risk flagged for fall.

findings.headline: EIA forecasts oil prices remain elevated until Hormuz flows normalize — global inventories drawing down
findings.source: EIA / Foreign Policy
findings.summary: US Energy Information Administration: 'Because of the large drawdown in global inventories triggered by continued disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, we forecast that oil prices will remain elevated until global oil flows return to normal and oil inventories are replenished.' Global oil inventories fell by average levels. Foreign Policy/Adam Tooze: war triggered surges in prices. Inflation 3.7%. Hormuz disruption feeding through to fertilizer, fuel, goods globally. No timeline for normalization.

findings.headline: SEC 'Regulation Crypto Assets' proposed Aug 18 — two exemptions ($5M startup, $75M fundraising), safe harbor
findings.source: SEC.gov / Federal Register / NatLawReview / Paul Hastings / Yahoo Finance / Crypto.news
findings.summary: SEC proposed August 18 comprehensive new offering and disclosure regime for crypto asset securities. Two exemptions: startup (up to $5M over 4 years) and fundraising (up to $75M in 12-month periods). Safe harbor for transition. Yahoo Finance: 'a future commission can withdraw that entire scheme with a memo because such legal interpretations aren't carved in stone.' Paul Hastings: Treasury issued proposed rulemaking for GENIUS Act implementation (Section 3 governing who may issue payment stablecoins). White House hosted crypto meeting urging Senate to pass CLARITY Act. Crypto.news: SEC, FASB, and OCC writing crypto rules through rulemaking instead of legislation. FASB proposed treating qualifying stablecoins as cash equivalents Aug 18.

findings.headline: CLARITY Act stalled — Senate missed August recess, odds collapsed to 16% (Galaxy: 10%), passage likely slips to 2027
findings.source: Tech Insider / Crypto News / Galaxy Digital / OneDayAdvisor / Medium
findings.summary: CLARITY Act passed House but has not completed Senate process. Senate filed cloture August 8 but no final floor vote. Missed August 10 recess deadline. Polymarket odds fell from 82% (February) to 16% (August 7). Galaxy Digital cut to 10%. OneDayAdvisor: 'faces its decisive Senate votes before the August 2026 recess' — outcome determining whether current agency classifications become permanent law. Medium: 'The Senate draft has not moved.' Passage likely slips to 2027. SEC, FASB, OCC writing rules through rulemaking instead. Regulatory uncertainty persists through Congressional inaction.

findings.headline: GENIUS Act stablecoin rules being finalized — Treasury seeking public comment, full effect expected early 2027
findings.source: Paul Hastings / Bitcoin.com / Medium / DeFi Education Fund
findings.summary: Treasury Department issued notice of proposed rulemaking seeking public comment on Section 3 of GENIUS Act — governing who may issue, offer, or sell payment stablecoins in US. DeFi Education Fund submitted comments on FinCEN direct relationships between stablecoin issuers and customers. Medium: stablecoin supply up 14% year on year but 'where does everything that is not a payment stablecoin live? The CLARITY Act was meant to sort tokens between SEC and CFTC. The Senate draft has not moved.' Bitcoin.com: stablecoin market peaked at $322.1B in mid-May, now declining as yield-seeking capital exits. Full GENIUS Act effect expected by early 2027.

findings.headline: Iran 6-month war mark — UN reports 56 executions on national security charges, 27 linked to protests, regime entrenched
findings.source: NPR / WSIU / KPBS / NCRI / CBS News / Wikipedia
findings.summary: Six months into war, Iran's regime remains entrenched despite original US goal of regime change. UN: executions surged — at least 56 executed on national security charges since mid-March, including 27 linked to protests earlier in 2026. NCRI: Resistance Units active, exhibition highlighted January 2026 uprising courage and sacrifices. Iran's leaders have 'dug in their heels and taken an even harder line.' War killed 3,375 Iranians, 33,000+ injured. 511+ total executions in 2026. 4,229+ protests. Iran's Pezeshkian previously said 'cannot continue with war forever' — internal pressure building from economic collapse + military losses + executions. But regime not collapsing.

findings.headline: Iran FM Araghchi open to diplomacy — 'pressure doesn't work' — but regime demands US change approach
findings.source: CBS News / Iran International / Reuters / Tribune
findings.summary: Iran Foreign Minister Araghchi posted on X: 'Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible. It hinges on U.S. understanding of one simple fact: pressure doesn't work.' Called for US to 'build trust, speak respectfully, acknowledge our rights, and uphold commitments.' Qatari PM in Tehran Thursday for talks on Hormuz. Iran's deputy FM insisted Hormuz won't reopen until US lifts blockade. Trump: 'not looking to meet' with Iran, argues naval blockade and sanctions have inflicted severe damage. Diplomatic efforts by Pakistan and Qatar have failed for months. Two-track: diplomatic track struggles while military hardliners push regime change. No breakthrough in sight.

findings.headline: Sen. Reed: 'Not a single objective has been achieved' in 6 months of Iran war
findings.source: CBS News / Sen. Reed statement
findings.summary: Sen. Jack Reed, top Democrat on Armed Services Committee, released blistering assessment: 'When he unilaterally launched this war, Trump promised he would destroy Iran's nuclear program, eliminate its missile and drone arsenal, dismantle its defense industrial base, wipe out its proxy networks, and topple the regime in a matter of weeks. Not a single objective has been achieved.' Political pressure building domestically as war drags on with no clear exit. Adds to institutional strain — munitions stockpiles dwindling, diplomatic staff only now returning.

findings.headline: WARSH HAWKISH — 2-year yield soars 8bp to 4.31%, September hike odds jump to 55.7%, stock market climbed
findings.source: CNBC / Bloomberg / Washington Post / Guardian / Google Finance
findings.summary: Market reaction to Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was immediate and significant. CNBC: 2-year Treasury yield soared ~8bp to 4.31% (highest since late July). September hike probability jumped to 55.7% (up ~20pp from prior day). Stock market indexes climbed after digesting speech. Google Finance: 'Stock Market News, Aug. 28, 2026: Warsh Comments Boost Rate-Hike' expectations. Bloomberg: key takeaways published. Washington Post: Warsh 'concerned about inflation, says bank may have work to do.' Guardian: Warsh argues recent softer data don't indicate 'underlying trends have meaningfully improved.' Heather Long: 'Warsh opened the door to a Fed rate hike. A hike probably won't come in September, but it will by October or December.' Cleveland Fed's Hammack: 'I believe it's time to act.'

findings.headline: Bitcoin loses $80,000 post-Warsh — profit-taking near $82K, 9-day ETF streak hits $3B but momentum moderating
findings.source: CoinDesk / Yahoo Finance / TradingKey / CoinPaper / CryptoNews / QCP / CoinStats
findings.summary: CoinDesk: Bitcoin traded near $80,000 then pulled back. Yahoo Finance: BTC at ~$79,500 on August 28, up +1.1% over 24h. Spot ETFs posted $242.3M net inflows on August 27 — 9th consecutive trading day, total streak $3B+. CoinPaper: Ark's ARKB added $29.7M, Bitwise BITB $21.7M, Grayscale Mini $11.7M. TradingKey: 'Bitcoin pulled back due to profit-taking near $80,000-$82,000 resistance zone. Leverage unwinding and moderated ETF flows reinforced intraday decline.' CoinStats: 'Risks: August 28 options expiry, macro surprises from Jackson Hole, profit-taking $80.5K-$82K, ETF demand may slow.' CryptoNews: max pain for Aug 28 expiry near $70K — $9-11K below spot. QCP: 'BTC enters Jackson Hole with stronger spot ETF flows, reduced futures leverage, supportive equity backdrop from Nvidia earnings.' CoinDesk: Warsh speech 'major event for bitcoin and gold' — could shape expectations for Fed support of Treasury buybacks. Coinbase: 'Bitcoin outperforming stocks and correlating with gold just when it matters most.' Arthur Hayes price target vs. rival investor saying policy move already 'collapsing under bond market pressure.'

findings.headline: China property crisis 6th year — Bloomberg: new credit support measures, Evergrande founder jailed for life, 'problem is systemic'

findings.summary: Bloomberg (Aug 28): China unveiled slew of measures to boost financing support for homebuyers and developers — latest attempt to put floor under 5-year property crisis. findings.headline: Japan yen carry trade risk heightened — BOJ September hike 84-85%, Tokyo core-core CPI at 2.0%, Warsh hawkish narrows spread
findings.source: FXStreet / ActionForex / Japan Times / Investing.com / CNBC / InvestingLive
findings.summary: Tokyo CPI data strengthens BOJ September hike case. Core CPI 1.8% (beat 1.7% forecast), core-core CPI hit 2.0% (BOJ target). ActionForex: 'Tokyo Core-Core CPI Hits 2% as September BoJ Hike Case Strengthens.' Markets pricing 84-85% probability. CNBC: Mizuho's Momma expects September hike, warns yen weakens if no hike. Investing.com: 'The End of Cheap Yen Could Mean Higher Yields for US Treasury.' Japan 10Y JGB yield approached 3% (highest since 1996), 30Y above 4%. US 30Y above 5.3%. Warsh hawkish speech raises US hike odds simultaneously — both central banks may tighten. Double-tightening = carry trade squeeze. This was the mechanism behind August 2024 crash, now replaying with larger scale and higher stakes. If US hikes AND Japan hikes, spread compresses from both sides.

findings.headline: France trading like periphery — OAT spreads widening, sovereign hierarchy breaking down

findings.summary: France starting to trade like the periphery. OAT widening becomes bigger European problem if it spreads to French bank credit, domestic equities, and peripheral sovereign spreads.
